If even one example fails, do not submit that code. Read the failing input and diagnostic, fix the underlying cause (not just the displayed output), and rerun `run_tests`; repeat until every example passes. Do not bypass the gate by submitting a guess, placeholder, or a different untested version, even if you are uncertain or unable to finish the derivation—use remaining calls to reason, test, or correct it instead. After the gate passes, make no code changes before submitting. A successful run is necessary but does not prove correctness: independently check the algorithm's invariant, worst-case complexity, and boundary cases from the constraints; when practical, compare against a simple brute-force/reference solution on small cases.
